prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market like a player: every 15 seconds after the open it looks at the market and answers the same question — buy UP, buy DOWN or pass right now. While holding, picking the other side sells the bet, picking the same side adds one more bet, and passing keeps it. Code only works out the facts for it, such as prices, costs and how the odds moved, and places the trades Jev decides on.
jev.archivedBanner: Viewing archived run {{n}}: it no longer bets, and its bets, decisions and scores stay as they ended.
jev.pnlLabel: PnL this run · settled bets, after fees
jev.scoreDetailsSub: How accurate is Jev's win chance? · {{n}} samples
jev.scoreDetailsSubDecisions: How often it traded, what it paid in fees, what holding would have done
jev.decisionStatsExplain: A look at Jev's trading itself. More trades mean more fees; "If all held" treats every settled buy as never sold and held to the close (buy fees still deducted). Compared with the actual PnL, it shows whether selling helped or hurt.
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Jev: lower than Market means Jev reads the window better than the market; lower than Math means it beats the formula that only looks at the gap and the time left. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: Jev's chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, and how many seconds after the open.
jev.guideDecides: The second line is Jev's decision and its confidence: flat or holding, it picks one of Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Pass. The "By the math" number after it is for you, not for Jev: on a buy, how much more each share of that side is worth than it costs (estimated win chance − ask − fee); on a hold or sell, how much more selling now gets per share than the estimate. The decision is Jev's.
jev.guideUpChance: The "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. Shown to you as a reference, not to Jev: it lags the market, and showing it to Jev pulled it into buying the side that had just been knocked down.
jev.guideJev: Jev's own win chance, R1–R3 only: in R2 and R3 it was also asked "will this settle UP?" and "will this settle DOWN?", averaged; in R1 it was the math chance adjusted by Jev's read of the move. It mostly restated whether the price was above or below the target, so R4 no longer asks.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideFold: Routine stay-out / hold rows are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click any row to see Jev's answer to every question.
jev.guideLegacy: R1–R3 are old versions: in R1 Jev picked the trade itself and judged whether the move still had legs; in R2 Jev only gave a win chance and code bet by comparing it with the asks; in R3 Jev was asked buy-or-not when flat and hold-or-sell when holding, what it saw included the math estimate and "X¢ cheaper than the estimate", and it was also asked who wins, for scoring only. Old runs are shown as they were.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.qEntryDesc: Asked at every checkpoint, flat or holding, and Jev sees the same thing either way: BTC against the target, time left, buying and selling on Binance, both sides' asks, bids and cost with the fee, and how both sides' odds moved over the last 30 seconds. If UP's price rose or fell {{jump}}¢ or more within 3 seconds in the last 15 seconds, it also says from what to what, how many seconds ago, and where it is now. Only facts, never cheap/expensive or should-buy conclusions. Jev picks one of the three and gives each a probability.
jev.guideBuy: When flat, code follows Jev's buy only when that pick has {{act}} or more (no less than all other picks combined), ${{stake}} a bet. Code only blocks mechanical problems: nobody selling that side, or a wallet that cannot afford a bet. When the wallet cannot afford a bet it stops itself until a new run.
jev.guideSell: While holding, the same question drives it: picking the other side sells every bet on this side (no flip in the same step; it is asked again next time); picking this side buys one more bet, up to ${{max}} on one side per window; passing, or a pick below {{act}}, keeps holding. With nobody bidding it is not asked and keeps holding.
jev.guideFill: Fills have a delay like a real order: {{delay}}s after Jev decides, code checks the book again and fills at that price if it is no more than {{tol}}¢ worse than what Jev saw; otherwise the trade is missed.

notice.MISSED_GONE: Missed: while waiting to fill, nobody was selling {{side}} any more (the ask was {{from}}¢)
notice.MISSED_SELL: Not sold: while waiting to fill, the bid moved from {{from}}¢ to {{to}}¢
notice.MISSED_SELL_GONE: Not sold: while waiting to fill, nobody was bidding any more (the bid was {{from}}¢)
notice.FILLED_AT: Expected to buy at {{from}}¢, filled at {{to}}¢
notice.SOLD_AT: Expected to sell at {{from}}¢, sold at {{to}}¢
